newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek central bank resorts to 12.4 pct o'night bid.
newsitem.headline: Greek central bank resorts to 12.4 pct o'night bid.

text.p: The Bank of Greece reverted to its 12.40 percent overnight bid today signalling that the recent liquidity shortage had run its course and depos and forex forwards were trading narrowly holding morning levels, dealers said.
Ecu/drachma eased at the central bank's fixing on the heels of renewed forex inflows estimated around 90 million ecus, dealers said.

"The highlight of the day was that the central bank resorted to its overnight bid at 12.40 percent pointing to a liquidity surplus, however marginal," said a a trader at a foreign bank. "The yield curve has little changed since this morning."
Other traders said they expected the short end of the yield curve to move gradually lower in the next few days as forex inflows continued but not a rate cut in the central bank's intervention rate.
"With inflation stuck at 8.5 percent, I do not think it is likely to see a rate cut in the central bank's intervention rate," said a trader at a private bank.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis is going to deliver his policy speech to parliament of Thursday.
The mark was quoted at 156.96/99 drachmas from Tuesday's 156.855 fix, the dollar at 239.91/96 drachmas from 240.100 and the Ecu at 300.32/42 from 300.500 drachmas.
"Inflows of 90 million ecus took place at the fixing driving ecu/drachma down," said a forex dealer.
